bug_report_content:
id: 1053
status: Fixed
summary: Overzealous optimization confuses variables
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 5
Comment 0 (2013-07-30): The following code: // ==ClosureCompiler== // @compilation_level ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS // ==/ClosureCompiler== var uid; function reset() { uid = Math.random(); } function doStuff() { reset(); var _uid = uid; if (uid < 0.5) { doStuff(); } if (_uid !== uid) { throw 'reset() was called'; } } doStuff(); ...gets optimized to: var a;function b(){a=Math.random();0.5>a&&b();if(a!==a)throw"reset() was called";}b(); Notice how _uid gets optimized away and (uid!==_uid) becomes (a!==a) even though doStuff() might have been called and uid's value may have changed and become different from _uid. As an aside, replacing the declaration with "var _uid = +uid;" fixes it, as does adding an extra "uid = _uid" after "var _uid = uid".
Comment 1 (2013-07-30): Thanks for the report!
Comment 2 (2013-08-08): Ya! Thanks for the nicely isolated bug report! Looks like a (non flow sensitive) variable inlining bug. After function inliner put down var _uid = uid = Math.random(), it might have gotten a bit too aggressive assuming _uid being replaceable by uid.
Comment 3 (2013-08-08): I have a patch that is currently in review. It should be fixed in the next release.
Comment 4 (2013-08-14): This issue was closed by revision 0123fd5303c8.
